messages.content: Let's continue a flaky test investigation.
Continuing a flaky test investigation.
Carry on.

We might revisit this next quarter. We can't call this finished while deduplicating the three near-identical workflows is missing. Once the release settles, pinning all third-party actions by digest is where attention goes. Had to untangle .github/dependabot.yml first.
What landed?
The bulk of the diff sits in Makefile. Thanks to required status checks on the default branch, the on-call pages stopped. Quarantining the six flakiest tests came off the board this morning.
Anything broken?
Buildx with a remote cache backend is the direction we committed to. .github/workflows/ci.yml grew by a couple hundred lines.
Anything broken?

Coverage reporting posted to the pull request has been live since Tuesday with no complaints. The trade-offs all pointed to ruff replacing flake8 and isort. Semantic versioning driven by commit messages is the direction we committed to.
How is a flaky test investigation going?
Splitting the linting job from the test job keeps getting pushed to next sprint.
Status please.
We can't call this finished while cutting the pipeline below eight minutes is missing.
Anything broken?
Artifact upload for the failing test logs is behind us now. The trade-offs all pointed to Codecov for coverage tracking.
Blockers?
The logs are easier to read now. Thanks to automated changelog generation on tag, the on-call pages stopped.
Where are we?
Parallel test execution across four shards held up fine through the whole load test. If this breaks later we can roll back.
I keep coming back to a required review from one code owner.
Makes sense, doing that.
